messages.content: Use web search to find relevant datasets. Only include landing pages or DOIs. Do not invent links. Do not call time, date, timestamp, or clock tools.

Query: Can you find datasets about Employment, Migration, Cultural activities and participation, Equality, inequality and social exclusion, and Economic conditions and indicators in German Democratic Republic (1949-1990) during the 1990s, matching this research need: survey data on foreign citizens in East Germany/GDR covering migration history, living conditions, employment and market-economy expectations, residence and citizenship plans, family situation, language skills, and relations with Germans
Respond ONLY as JSON in this exact shape: {"items":[{"title":"...","url_or_doi":"...","justification":"..."}]}. Put any DOI, URL, landing page, or link in url_or_doi.

queries: GESIS Ausländer DDR 1990 Befragung Lebensbedingungen Marktwirtschaft Erwartungen Staatsbürgerschaft Deutschkenntnisse
survey foreign citizens GDR 1990 migration history market economy expectations relations Germans dataset

content.text: {"items":[{"title":"Ausländer in Ostdeutschland 1990 (Foreigners in Eastern Germany 1990) — GESIS Study ZA6342","url_or_doi":"https://access.gesis.org/dbk/4804","justification":"Excellent match and the most directly relevant dataset. Conducted in 1990 by the Berliner Institut für Sozialwissenschaftliche Studien (BISS), this survey examines foreign citizens living in East Germany during the transition from the GDR to reunified Germany. It covers migration behavior, reasons for immigration, living conditions, and relationships between Germans and foreigners. The study includes 327 foreign respondents (114 variables) and a comparison group of 173 German respondents (104 variables). Foreign respondents included Soviet, Vietnamese, Polish, and Hungarian citizens, primarily residing in East Berlin and Dresden. Particularly relevant for investigating migration histories, employment and socioeconomic circumstances, residence status, integration, and attitudes toward German society. Its timing also makes it valuable for studying foreign citizens' experiences during the transition to a market economy. The dataset is archived by GESIS under study number ZA6342."}]}
